key_insight: Experimentally trained surrogate models can forecast cylinder-wake evolution faster than real time, but they mainly retain low-frequency flow dynamics and lose transient/high-frequency detail as uncertainty increases.
engineering_relevance: The study shows these models could support real-time flow prediction and control in practical engineering settings where measurements are noisy, sparse, and incomplete.
method: Forecasted 2D, 2-component PIV velocity fields from subcritical cylinder-wake experiments.
Compared fully convolutional networks, U-Nets, Fourier neural operators, and DMD-based models.
Tested short-to-long forecast horizons at Re=590 and across Re=230–2920.
evidence_signal: Across experimentally measured datasets, the models produced useful short-horizon forecasts and faster-than-real-time evaluation, but performance degraded with noisy, incomplete observations and more complex flows.
watch_item: These surrogates may underrepresent transient structures and high-frequency energy, so they should not be relied on for fine-scale flow details without uncertainty-aware validation.
paper_title: Data-driven surrogate models for forecasting experimentally measured fluid flows
